The 2026 World Series was the championship series of Major League Baseball's (MLB) 2026 season. The 122nd edition of the World Series, the best-of-seven playoff series was played from October 23 to 28 by the American League (AL) champion Tampa Bay Rays and the National League (NL) champion Milwaukee Brewers. The Brewers defeated the Rays in five games to win their first championship in franchise history. Brewers catcher William Contreras was named the World Series Most Valuable Player (MVP) after batting .381 and going 10-for-13 on Automated Ball-Strike System (ABS) challenges in the series. 
The Brewers and Rays both sought their first World Series championship. The Brewers swept the Los Angeles Dodgers to win their first National League pennant, and their second pennant after winning in the American League in 1982. The Rays won their third American League pennant after defeating the Cleveland Guardians in six games, and their first since 2020. The Brewers had home-field advantage due to their league-best win–loss record. 
The first two games saw narrow Brewers victories. In Game 1, the Brewers maintained an early lead to win 3–2. In Game 2, they overcame the Rays' four runs in the first inning to win 5–4. In Game 3, the Brewers blew out the Rays, scoring 10 runs by the fifth inning and winning 10–1. Tampa Bay's lone win came in Game 4, when pinch hitter Ben Williamson hit a walk-off single in the twelfth inning for a 4–3 comeback victory. Milwaukee closed the series in Game 5, maintaining another early lead to win 4–1 and clinch their first title.
